nb_eye_of_the_needle_area.blurb: A stretch of Walton Glen Canyon, New Brunswick, where the walls pinch to roughly 10 feet apart, and the home of eleven water ice lines. Climbs are strung along the brook from the narrow point up toward the Sea Monster Wall. The grades are moderate to serious: one WI2, a handful of WI3 lines, about as many WI4, and two WI5 pitches, so most days suit a leader comfortable on steeper ice. The longest line here runs three pitches of blue ice, while shorter ones are one-rope affairs. Getting into the canyon is a real commitment, with a steep descent, stream crossings and rope work reported, so plan for a full day and bring a dozen screws.
